svg.title: Where copies of a note exist, and who holds the key to each
svg.desc: Left: an iCloud note exists on your Mac, on your iPhone and on Apple's servers. Under Standard Data Protection the key to the server copy is held by Apple; with Advanced Data Protection it is held only by your trusted devices. Right: a note in a local app such as an On My Mac account or Cyanote exists in one place, a file on your own disk, protected by FileVault and, for a locked note, by its own password.
svg.text: Every copy of a note is a copy someone could read
Encryption decides who holds the key to each copy. A copy that never exists needs no key.
An iCloud note: three or more copies
Your Mac
key: FileVault
Your iPhone
key: its passcode
Apple's servers
key: see below
Standard (the default)
Apple holds the server key and can decrypt the note
Advanced Data Protection
only your trusted devices hold it
Locked notes are end-to-end encrypted under either setting.
A local note: one copy
A file on your own disk
key: FileVault, plus a password if locked
On My Mac notes in Apple Notes,
or an app with no sync such as Cyanote
No server copy. Backups are your job.
